rationale:
Evidence. The best raced design is iteration 1 (score 154.1): sensors at x = -0.04..+0.04 spaced 0.02 m, all at y = 0.03, sensor_size 0.012, kp 3.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.4. Line loss stayed at about 1.0 per run on every track in iterations 1 to 5, whatever the spread, footprint or kp. Iteration 2 (kp 3.5) fell to 125.8, iteration 3 (16 mm footprint) to 149.8, and iteration 4 (narrow spread) to 133.9. Iteration 5 (kd 0.35, the approved input entityR1) scored 89.2. Its oval progress fell from 0.67 to 0.41, and only steering oscillation fell (0.30 to 0.23), so lower kd hurts tracking. The entityR1 feedback says that design has not raced; the race data now shows it did, so that feedback is out of date. Oscillation of 0.11 to 0.30 shows under-correction, not instability. Speed is not the limit: the oval finish time was 1.93 s at base_speed 1.4.

Change. I return kd to 0.5 and keep the iteration 1 geometry and controller gains. The one new variable is a forward sensor offset: the two outer sensors move from y = 0.03 to y = 0.05, with the inner three at y = 0.03. This gives earlier sight of the tape on bend entry, the lever the Evaluator named after kd was ruled out. kp 3.0, ki 0.05, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction, sensor_size 0.012 and the body and wheel values are unchanged, so the effect is read against 154.1.

Hypotheses. (a) Outer sensors further forward see the tape earlier, so line-loss events fall below about 0.9 per run on the s-bend and slalom. (b) If line loss stays at about 1.0, the cause is not sensing lead, and the next test should be ki or a change to the line-loss behaviour.

Expected result. A score near or above 154, with line loss below 1.0 and progress on the s-bend and slalom at least as high as iteration 1. Risk: a forward offset changes the signal phase, so it may raise oscillation on the oval above 0.30. If so, revert the outer sensors to y = 0.03 before changing gains.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track.
